body.statement: The construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} embeds a relatively open family \(\{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\). For every admissible \(\rho\) and \(x\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals are identical across \(\rho\), whereas \[m_1^{P_\rho}(x)=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]=1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),\qquad \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).\] Hence there are interior \(\rho_0,\rho_1\in\mathcal R\) with \(\rho_0(z_0)\ne\rho_1(z_0)\) such that \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho_0})=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho_1})\), and their conditional return-coordinate marginals are also identical, but \[|\tau_{n,P_{\rho_1}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho_0}}(z_0)|=a_{\mathrm w}^2|\rho_1(z_0)-\rho_0(z_0)|>0.\] Therefore \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\). This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; the full historical wealth panel may distinguish the two laws.
body.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
body.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving full-panel identification under event transport.
body.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.
